observation_summary: The compiler fails to resolve type aliases when they are used in JSDoc annotations before their definition within a goog.scope block, resulting in an 'Unknown type' error.
hypothesis: The alias resolution mechanism in ScopedAliases was incorrectly tied to the order of traversal, failing to identify aliases defined later in the scope when encountering them in JSDoc annotations earlier in the scope.
prediction: The fix will introduce a pre-processing step to identify all aliases within a scope before attempting to resolve them, ensuring that aliases are available regardless of their definition order.
experiment_rationale: The diff shows the addition of a 'findAliases' method that iterates over all variables in the scope to populate the 'aliases' map before processing the nodes, which confirms that the original algorithm was order-dependent and insufficient.
reasoning_summary: The bug is an algorithmic deficiency in how aliases are discovered and mapped. The original implementation attempted to identify aliases on-the-fly during traversal, which failed for forward references. The fix implements a more robust two-pass approach (or a pre-scan) to ensure all aliases are known before they are used, which is a correction of the procedural logic for alias resolution.
evidence_used: The diff adds a 'findAliases' method that iterates over all variables in the scope.
The diff removes the logic that attempted to identify aliases only when visiting specific nodes during traversal.
The bug report states that aliases cannot be used before their definitions, indicating an order-of-operations issue in the algorithm.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves managing the relationship between aliases and their definitions, the root cause is the procedural logic (the algorithm) used to discover these aliases during the traversal of the AST.
